images.title: From rows of squares to bars
images.purpose: Show that a row of squares stands up as a bar of the same height: Reading 3, Playing 5 and Helping at home 2, each with a dotted arrow from its row to its bar.
images.composition: On the left three rows of teal squares (1 square = 1 hour), on the right the same data as a bar graph with the vertical line marked 0 to 6, and one dotted arrow from each row to the top of its bar.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816, in two parts. LEFT PART, rows of squares: the caption 1 square = 1 hour left-aligned at x 40, centred on y 95 (dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif, 36 px). Three rows, each with its name above it (left-aligned at x 40, dark #1F2937 bold, 34 px) and, below the name, a line of squares, each square 70 by 70 px, teal #0072B2 with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline (3 px), 8 px apart, the first at x 40. From the top: Helping at home at y 185 with exactly 2 squares (x 40 to 188, y 210 to 280); Playing at y 335 with exactly 5 squares (x 40 to 422, y 360 to 430); Reading at y 485 with exactly 3 squares (x 40 to 266, y 510 to 580). In all 10 squares. RIGHT PART, the bar graph: the label Number of Hours centred at (780, 95) in dark #1F2937 bold (36 px); a vertical line (dark #2B2B2B, 4 px) at x 780 from y 620 up to y 130, with exactly 7 marks: a short tick (14 px) to the left of the line at every whole number from 0 to 6 (0 at y 620 and one mark every 80 px up, so 6 is at y 140), each mark numbered 0 to 6 at its left (right-aligned to x 750, dark #1F2937 bold, 32 px); a horizontal base line (dark #2B2B2B, 4 px) at y 620 from x 780 to x 1400. Exactly 3 bars, all 120 px wide, filled amber #E69F00 with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline (3 px), standing on the base: Reading: x 860 to 980, y 380 to 620 (height 240 px, which is 3 on the vertical line); Playing: x 1040 to 1160, y 220 to 620 (height 400 px, which is 5 on the vertical line); Helping at home: x 1220 to 1340, y 460 to 620 (height 160 px, which is 2 on the vertical line). Under the base, centred under each bar, its name in dark #1F2937 (32 px, first line at y 665). The base is labelled Activities, centred at (1110, 765) in dark #1F2937 bold (36 px); the name Helping at home is written on two lines, Helping over at home. ARROWS: exactly 3 dotted arrows in reddish purple #CC79A7 (round dots 4 px, about 8 px apart), each a smooth curve with a small solid arrowhead (18 px) at its end, joining a row to its bar without touching any number, name or square, and not crossing each other. Arrow 1 starts at (204, 245) just right of the Helping at home row, crosses the vertical line at y 178 (between the marks 5 and 6), peaks near (1044, 140) and comes down onto the top of the Helping at home bar at (1280, 450). Arrow 2 starts at (438, 395) just right of the Playing row, crosses the vertical line at y 248 (between the marks 4 and 5), peaks near (1046, 176) and comes down onto the top of the Playing bar at (1100, 212). Arrow 3 starts at (282, 545) just right of the Reading row, crosses the vertical line at y 334 (between the marks 3 and 4), peaks near (865, 318) and comes down onto the top of the Reading bar at (920, 372). In all there are 3 rows (10 squares), 3 bars and 3 arrows. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a bar whose height differs from its row of squares (3, 5 and 2), or a row with a square count other than 2, 5 and 3
arrows that cross each other, that cover a number or a name, or that join a row to the wrong bar
a number written on a bar or a total anywhere in the frame
images.takeaway: A row of squares stands up as a bar of the same height, so the height of a bar tells the number of hours.
images.description: Three rows of squares (Helping at home 2, Playing 5, Reading 3) on the left and the same data as bars of height 3, 5 and 2 on a bar graph on the right, joined by dotted arrows.
images.context: Concept image for From Squares to Bars. It follows the idea of the book's two recordings of a day (a table of squares and a bar graph) and uses the numbers of this concept's own example: Kabir's Saturday with reading 3, playing 5 and helping at home 2.
images.teaching_notes: The rows are listed from the top as Helping at home, Playing, Reading only so that the three dotted arrows do not cross. Let the student follow each arrow and compare the number of squares with the height of the bar. The slip to watch: thinking a wider bar shows a bigger number.

image_decisions.why: The rows of squares beside the bar graph, joined by dotted arrows, show that a row stands up as a bar of the same height.
